host: Apple M4 (shared; load average 8-11 during every run), macOS; Node v26.8.1; cargo release
workload: NFCorpus campaign input (3633 one-chunk documents, storeText false, chunkWords 4096; 324 queries, k=100, candidateLimit=100, lexicalWeight 1, semanticWeight 0), 8 passes = 2592 queries

rust_microbench.levers: dense slot-to-position table (hash map beyond 2^19 slots), closure posting decode with a single-byte varint fast path, u32 captured postings, slot word counts kept by the store so scoring never touches a document, packed (score, index) selection

node_end_to_end.script: bench.cjs in this directory: memorizeDocuments then 2592 searchDocuments calls, hrtime per call, RSS sampled every 64 calls
node_end_to_end.note: v37 = V37 capsule package (async napi path); v38 = this tree (packed synchronous path through index.js); v38raw = this tree through the untouched async native method; after_gc fields from node --expose-gc

finding: Rust search time drops about 1.5x; end-to-end Node query time drops 2.2-2.6x with the packed synchronous result path (p50 97 us -> 33-40 us). Peak RSS on macOS is 6-7 MB higher on the packed path than on the async path of the same binary (117 vs 110-111 MB; JS heap after GC identical at 11 MB), so the delta is native allocator residency on the main thread; the Linux campaign (serving-v38-monotonic-v1 on writerslogic-02) is the matched measurement that decides acceptance.
